sam_c: Hey @ian_support — customer reported a big token billing mismatch. Their client SDK shows ~430 tokens for a chat request but the invoice shows ~720. They use streaming + function calls and include a system message. Can we triage?

ian_support: Thanks Sam. Can you paste a redacted request + the invoice lines (or invoice id)? Also did customer disconnect early or cancel streams?

sam_c: Invoice id: INV-9921 (redacted). Customer pasted this curl they used: 

kevin_sdk: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-rev-3","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that logs everything."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this long doc..."}],"stream":true,"functions":[{"name":"lookup","parameters":{"type":"object"}}]}'
```

kevin_sdk: Their client-side token estimator (our JS SDK) returns: prompt 140 tokens, estimated completion 290 -> 430 total. But billing shows 720 tokens. Customer says they stopped the stream after receiving first chunk.

jordan_ml: Two quick possibilities: 1) Server-side metering counts all tokens generated server-side (including function call args, tool outputs, hidden/system inserts) even if the client disconnects mid-stream — those tokens are still billed. 2) The SDK estimator doesn't account for internal server-inserted system text or function-call expansion.

ophelia_sre: Confirming SRE note: our metering service logs final generation length based on the generator state, not what was streamed to the socket. If the generator continued after client disconnect, it will show up on the invoice. We also append an internal audit system message in some private stacks which can add ~20-60 tokens depending on model.

metering-bot: Automated note: metering-record created for req_id=req_0a1b2c3d, billed_tokens=720, model=gpt-rev-3, prompt_tokens=160, completion_tokens=560, includes_function_output=true

ian_support: Kevin — can you repro locally with stream and then force-close the connection to see what our SDK estimator counts vs the server metering? If you can capture req_id from gateway logs that helps.

kevin_sdk: Repro steps I used: 
1) Run this curl with stream=true.
2) After first chunk arrives, Ctrl-C to close connection.
3) Check server logs: 
```
2026-02-21T14:12:10Z req=req_0a1b2c3d stream: client disconnected, generator continued, final_tokens=560
```
4) SDK estimator returned 430 but meter service logged 720.

jordan_ml: Here's why the numbers differ in more detail: the SDK local tokenizer only tokenizes the message payloads you pass (system+user+assistant) and predicted generation. It does NOT include: 
- server-side inserted control tokens (hidden system/prompt augmentations)
- function call serialization and the tool/plugin output tokens (we execute tools server-side and then embed their outputs)
- tokens generated after the client disconnects but produced by the generator pipeline
Also note model-specific tokenization changes (new merges) can shift counts by a few percent.

kevin_sdk: Example: customer called a function that returned a large JSON blob. SDK estimate ignored the full function output because in streaming mode the app dropped the connection early, but the function output was still produced and counted by the server.

sam_c: The customer is upset because they were billed for tokens they "never received". What's our policy?

ian_support: Policy: we bill for model work performed (generation + tooling). If generation completed on server side, it's billable even if the client dropped the socket. We should explain and show logs. But we can offer a one-time goodwill credit if this is the first incident.

ophelia_sre: Action items for SRE/eng:
- Add a metering debug endpoint to correlate req_id -> streamed bytes vs generated tokens.
- Add note in SDK docs about estimator limitations (hidden system tokens, server-side tool outputs, disconnect behavior).
- Investigate whether generator can cancel work on abrupt client disconnects (opt-in experimental).

kevin_sdk: I'll attach a minimal repro gist and the SDK's local estimator output. Suggest adding an optional flag to SDK to include function output estimation if users register tool schemas.

jordan_ml: For now to respond to the customer: show req_id logs (we have generator final_tokens), explain difference, offer 50% credit on the invoiced delta if they're a small customer. Also include steps they can take to reduce future delta: disable large sync tools, avoid abrupt disconnects, or set lower max_tokens on the request.

sam_c: I'll send the logs + explanation and propose the credit. Thanks everyone.

ophelia_sre: Noted, opening an internal ticket to track the SRE work: SRE-3452.

metering-bot: Ticket created: SRE-3452 (link redacted)
